summary: The note tours a year of seasonal family celebrations around the world, showing how households give traditional recipes an eco-friendly twist through organic, local, plant-based, foraged, fermented and energy-saving methods. Examples range from a North Carolina apple pie bake-off to Nowruz in London, Midsummer in Stockholm and a communal spring feast in Caserta. It concludes that the best family recipes delight the palate, nourish the body and respect the earth.
one_line: Families worldwide adapt festive seasonal recipes with sustainable ingredients and methods, from autumn apple pies to Midsummer foraging and communal spring feasts.
key_facts: On September 14, 2023, the Jackson family of Asheville, North Carolina, gathered apples from their backyard orchard for their annual apple pie bake-off.
The Jackson family used organically grown Granny Smith and Honeycrisp apples and Grandma Edith's recipe, swapping refined sugars for natural maple syrup and using whole wheat flour.
On December 25, 2023, the Moreau family in Quebec, Canada, served Réveillon, the traditional Christmas Eve dinner, with a sustainable seafood stew of locally caught fish and shellfish.
Marie-Claude Moreau, the Moreau family matriarch, hunts for ingredients that support local fishers and are environmentally responsible.
On March 21, 2024, the Patel family, living in London with roots in Tehran, prepared a plant-based Nowruz feast; their sabzi polo uses bioengineered plant-based alternatives to fish.

On July 4, 2024, the Oluwaseyi family in Lagos, Nigeria, grilled agro-ecologically farmed chicken with organically sourced traditional Yoruba spices and served salads of indigenous vegetables from their urban home garden.
The Diop family of Dakar, Senegal, uses slow cookers and pressure cookers to make peanut stew (mafé) with reduced energy for their April 5, 2024, Senegalese Independence Day.
The Murthy family of Mysore, India, uses solar energy to cook Pongal rice for the Sankranthi festival on January 15, 2024.
Michael and Sophie Bernstein of Stockholm, Sweden, foraged berries, edible flowers and greens from local woodlands for their Midsummer's Eve Smörgåsbord on June 24, 2024.
The Kim family from Busan, South Korea, celebrated Chuseok on September 9, 2023, with kimchi made from locally grown napa cabbage and spices fermented in onggi pots.
Fermentation enhances flavor and nutritional value and preserves food while reducing reliance on refrigeration and chemical additives.
On May 20, 2024, Paolo Rossi and his neighbors in Caserta, Italy, prepared a communal feast for La Festa della Primavera, with pasta and homemade sauces from community garden produce.
